title: Quarantining an inbox item does NOT release its continuation-registry binding — adopted continuations re-dispatch parked/consumed scopes forever; plus no operator command exists for registry lifecycle
summary: Live burn (batch-20260816b cycle-1487): context-fill-telemetry-and-cap was parked out of .evolve/inbox (tracked deletion shipped d3c69cd2) after 2 lane burns — yet the next wave dispatched it ANYWAY as an ADOPTED continuation from continuation-registry.json (cycle-1484's binding), burned a 3rd full lane on the same deterministic test collision, and RE-REGISTERED itself (9813bc621fe4) for a 4th. The dispatch pool is TWO stores — inbox items and scope-keyed continuation bindings — and quarantine only touched one. Console had to hand-edit the registry under its flock sidecar because no evolve command manages it. CORRECTED third observation: during the cycle-1493 halt, sibling lane cycle-1494 initially LOOKED unpreserved (no binding, uncommitted worktree) but in fact DRAINED to PASS and shipped 4f133efe — the halt stops new dispatch, live lanes drain. No halt-path preservation defect demonstrated; the transient console misread is recorded so the drain semantics are known: mid-drain state inspection is unreliable evidence of orphaning. FOURTH burn + source pinned (batch-20260816d cycle-1497): the CONSUMED sleep-time scope was re-dispatched with NO adoption event and NO carryover entry (both verified empty) — the WAVE PLANNER itself mints lanes from registry bindings, so the registry is a first-class lane SOURCE, not merely a resume detail. Guard must sit at the PLANNER'S registry read (skip + release scopes with no live pending item) as the primary fix; the post-triage adoption guard is the secondary belt.
root_cause: Registry lifecycle is one-sided: WriteRegistryEntry runs at every abnormal cycle end, DeleteRegistryEntry exists (added for the 2026-08-10 immortal-entries stall) but nothing invokes it when an item leaves the pending pool (consumed, parked, superseded). The adopted-continuation path checks only the registry, not whether the scope id still has a live inbox item — so any scope whose item is retired keeps re-spawning lanes from its preserved snapshot.
fix: (1) Transactional retire: wherever an item leaves the pending pool (ship-time consumption in phases/ship/consume.go, inbox-mover promote/park paths), call continuation.DeleteRegistryEntry for the item id — preserving the binding VALUE into the item file (released_continuations[] annotation, as done manually 2026-08-16) so salvage pointers survive. (2) PLANNER source guard (primary): the wave planner's registry-scope minting must verify the scope id resolves to a live pending item — a miss logs, releases the binding, and the lane slot goes to real backlog. (2b) Adoption guard (belt): before adopting a continuation, verify the scope id resolves to a live pending item; a miss logs and releases the binding instead of dispatching. (3) Operator surface: `evolve continuation list` + `evolve continuation release <scope-id>` using the existing package functions (registry.go) under the flock convention — console should never flock-edit JSON by hand. Red-first: fixture where a scope is parked then a wave plans — adopted-continuation dispatch must NOT occur; binding is released with the annotation.
files: go/internal/continuation/registry.go (Delete exists, uncalled from lifecycle paths)
go/internal/phases/ship/consume.go (consumption must also release the binding)
acceptance: Parking or consuming an item releases its registry binding in the same operation, with the binding value preserved into the item file (no pointer loss).
Adoption path refuses a binding whose scope id has no live pending item (logged, binding released) — red-first on the cycle-1487 shape.
evolve continuation list/release work under the flock sidecar; release annotates the item file.
go vet + touched suites + -race green; wiring proof at all lifecycle call sites.
connects_to: PR #466 transactional inbox consumption (same disease one store over: lifecycle acts must be transactional with ALL dispatch-relevant state)
2026-08-10 immortal-registry-entries stall (DeleteRegistryEntry's origin; this closes its remaining unreachable half)

notes: Filed after console-side manual remediation: bindings for context-fill-telemetry-and-cap (cycle-1487), minted-phase-verdict-contract-unsatisfiable (1483), dead-api-sweep (1483) released under the registry flock, pointers preserved in the item files. The pattern to generalize: the pending pool has THREE dispatch sources and every retirement path must retire from all of them. | REPRIORITIZED 2026-08-17 0.86->0.89 per docs/incidents/2026-08-17-failure-rate-review-1481-1503.md ranked plan (operator directive: prioritize pipeline/fail-rate improvements).
